punchline: A hospital cut soda sales without saying a word, just by putting water in the fridge next to the till.
thirty_sec: At Massachusetts General Hospital, Dr Anne Thorndike changed one thing in the cafeteria. The fridges by the cash registers, which held only soda, got water too, and baskets of bottled water went next to the food stations. Nobody was told. Over three months, soda sales fell 11.4 percent and water sales rose 25.8 percent. James Clear's point is that we often pick things because of where they are, so put the good option within reach.
